## docs/STAR_PATROL.md
SHA-256: 2ee6886b9e6acbd6127c63cb0aba765a0c1805c972dfee0e18e0d4aba907df55
~~~text
    1 | # Star Patrol combat update
    2 | 
    3 | Marked gold supply ships carry a visible reward icon and drop a real falling capsule when defeated. Every eighth ordinary kill also adds randomized gear. Loot persists between levels, expires if missed and gently attracts toward a nearby ship in the collection area. Score is earned through combat; no automatic gear is awarded just for reaching a level.
    4 | 
    5 | - Cannons stack through twin, triple and five-shot tiers. Damage removes one tier.
    6 | - Rapid fire lasts 14 seconds; piercing lasers 16; wingmates 18. Repeated temporary pickups stack up to 24 seconds. Shields absorb one hit.
    7 | - Lives come only from supply ships on six-level milestones, at least 90 gameplay seconds apart. Four lives maximum; already-full life pickups become shields. Ordinary loot never includes lives.
    8 | - Level 2 introduces armor, level 3 aimed gunners, and every fourth level an armored ace with fan attacks and a laser reward. Formation speed, projectile speed, firing rate and enemy durability increase within bounds. Charged shots have a visible warning.
    9 | 
   10 | Rendering retains the pastel/outlined visual identity, with compact level/weapon badges, timed-gear bars, companion and shield indicators, collectible icons and brief pickup feedback. Touch steering/firing and keyboard arrows/A/D + Space remain supported. Pause freezes combat and gear durations.
   11 | 
   12 | The module stays lazy. No dependencies, extra render loops or standalone physics engine were added. Fixed pools reserve 52 player and 28 enemy projectiles, eight pickups and 24 short effects. Swept collisions handle angled shots and nearest-hit ordering; piercing shots cannot repeatedly damage the same ship. Use numeric `?aiSeed=42` in development for reproducible attack/loot choices.
   13 | 
   14 | ## Verification
   15 | 
   16 | - Full Vitest suite: **297 tests across 32 files passed**. After the final allocation reduction, both affected suites passed again (**51 tests**).
   17 | - Nine dedicated combat tests cover formations through level 20, loot on kills, life restrictions, weapon tiers/durations, piercing collisions, attack warnings, shields/damage, transition cleanup and 100 seeded powered scenarios.
   18 | - Four browser checks passed: real touch/keyboard play at small viewport sizes; actual drops/catches and progression to level 2; pause/resume and listener disposal; production mobile/desktop launch; registry laziness, navigation cycles and arcade exclusion from tournaments.
   19 | - Production TypeScript/Vite build and bundle guard passed. Game implementation remains a dynamic entry; application shell is **23,998 gzip bytes**, below its existing 24,000-byte budget. Shared Phaser remains the dominant initial payload.
   20 | - Mobile and desktop screenshots were inspected. Android hardware and sustained on-device 60 FPS have **not** been verified; no such performance claim is made. Higher endless levels have scenario coverage rather than exhaustive human playtesting.
   21 | 
   22 | An initial navigation run timed out; its isolated rerun and the final complete browser group passed without changes to shared navigation. A browser run interrupted by source hot reload was discarded and repeated after edits stopped. Math Quiz and other game implementations were not modified.
~~~

    1 | # Lost Temple AI correction — 16 October 2026
    2 |

Temple resting points also clear the moving-boulder sweep and quicksand; a two-stage upper approach crosses the quicksand instead of waiting inside it. Original course geometry, hazards, limits and human/AI physics remain unchanged. AI still executes only legal simulated shots through its existing cancellable worker.

    8 | 
    9 | - Eleven targeted unit tests pass: static waypoint clearance, the reaction-delay regression, and nine full legal tee-to-cup simulations covering Medium/Hard/Impossible at seeds 11, 42 and 123. Both outer plates are required and verified; repeated ineffective shots are rejected by the regression.
   10 | - Three actual browser worker runs completed Lost Temple at seed 123: Medium 15 strokes, Hard 18, Impossible 12, all within the ordinary 27-stroke limit. No position resets, fabricated scores or authored shot velocities were used. These are bounded practical planners, not a guarantee for every possible seed.
   11 | - The complete 276-test unit suite and production build passed. Golf navigation, SVG course previews and mobile course selection were also checked. The four portrait previews are generated from the actual course geometry without initializing gameplay.
   12 | - Happy Birds received a presentation-only pass: round bodies, oval wings, soft sky/clouds and removal of the nested box frame. Shared-arena physics, controls, timer and AI remain intact; existing touch/pause/deadlock browser checks pass and final visuals were inspected.

## docs/ULTIMATE_GOLF.md
SHA-256: c1a1c9b1257c97eecb5ef05c0accb4b5acfd4b972a90497f6420f62274582546
~~~text
    1 | # Ultimate Golf port
    2 | 
    3 | Source studied: [abdullah-b41/L1T1-Game-Project](https://github.com/abdullah-b41/L1T1-Game-Project), commit `06dcdc65b06e9767e9089a032f1e465fe8ee931b`, local `~/Documents/Game-References/Ultimate-Golf/the_ultimate_golf/the_ultimate_golf.c` (6,015 lines). The source credits Abdullah Al Nafi and Syed Abdul Fahim. The reference repository was not modified; its pre-existing untracked `.DS_Store` and `the_ultimate_golf/game` remain unchanged.
    4 | 
    5 | This is a native TypeScript/Phaser rewrite, with no C executable, raylib dependency, original textures, music or sounds. Original course geometry and mechanics are expressed as data and small simulation classes. All displayed artwork is original Phaser Graphics/SVG, using Pocket Rivals' palette, type and UI.
    6 | 
    7 | ## Courses and mechanics
    8 | 
    9 | | Original course | Ported elements                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
   10 | | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   11 | | Foundry         | Six serpentine lanes, crate, diamond, alternating girders, bumpers, oil, two conveyor belts, rotating cross, three moving beams, magnetic attraction/core, extending piston, three lava pools, timed laser                                                     |
   12 | | Shoreline       | Ten islands/paths, soft and wet sand, tidal bridges and opposing currents, flowing ford, whirlpools, four moving crabs, palms, spring bumpers                                                                                                                  |
   13 | | Event Horizon   | Eleven platforms, low-friction vacuum strips, solar wind, two gravity planets and black-hole field, three directed portal pairs, four asteroids, phased lasers, rotating cross, bumpers, recurring UFO visits with lift and safe adjacent-platform drop                |
   14 | | Lost Temple     | Thirteen walls, river and two five-plank bridges with different collapse delays/regeneration, mud, moss, quicksand, three rolling boulders, four phased dart gates, rotating cross, bumpers, six-second entrance plate/gate, two latched plates and inner gate |
   15 | 
   16 | Course coordinates, tee/cup positions and obstacle dimensions retain the source's 1920×1080 units. Portrait screens rotate the course clockwise; landscape uses the source orientation. A responsive DOM header/footer reserves real touch targets and spacing, and the remaining viewport uses one uniform camera scale. Full view fits the course; Focus magnifies the ball neighborhood to a readable scale (2.2–4×), follows smoothly and clamps to world bounds. Input uses the exact inverse transform; the camera stays still during a drag. There is no independent X/Y scaling or clipped permanent footer text.
   17 | 
   18 | Mouse and touch share one pointer-owned drag path. Pull back anywhere inside the course and release; drag displacement determines direction and power. Use Focus or F for detail, Retry or R to restart, ? for course help, and Escape/back for the shared pause menu. A canceled/interrupted gesture never shoots.
   19 | 
   20 | ## Original rules retained
   21 | 
   22 | Ball radius 7; maximum speed 650; pullback multiplier 3.125; minimum pullback 14 world units; normal friction 110; stop threshold 6. Special surfaces and forces override these as in the source. The cup captures within the original 16.5×16.5 box; no invented speed condition is added. Moving obstacles transfer legal relative momentum. Hazards return the ball to a safe last-shot position and do not add another stroke.
   23 | 
   24 | | Challenge | Obstacle speed | Stroke factor | Preview | Completion scoring         |
   25 | | --------- | -------------- | ------------- | ------- | -------------------------- |
   26 | | Easy      | 0.7×           | 1.5×          | 0.6 s   | 100 + 10 per unused stroke |
   27 | | Normal    | 1×             | 1.1×          | 0.3 s   | 250 + 25 per unused stroke |
   28 | | Hard      | 1.3×           | 0.75×         | Off     | 500 + 50 per unused stroke |
   29 | 
   30 | Base limits are 18, 25, 20, 18; rounding follows the C implementation. Winning on the last stroke succeeds before the exhausted-stroke check. Best scores for each course persist under `pocket-rivals.ultimate-golf.v1`; Finish run records their sum through the shared Arcade result screen. All four courses are available immediately, matching the source level picker. Next course provides sequential progression.
   31 | 
   32 | ## Reliability adaptations and scope
   33 | 
   34 | - Fixed 240 Hz simulation replaces variable frame substeps. Projection uses separating contact normals, and all forces/collisions respect the speed cap. Obstacle contact velocity follows its actual difficulty-scaled motion.
   35 | - Aiming uses the drag displacement from the initial pointer rather than requiring the finger to cover the tiny ball. It preserves power units and makes the same controls practical on mobile.
   36 | - Focus is optional; the overview always shows the complete course. The ball has a visibility halo without enlarging its collision radius.
   37 | - UFO carrying suspends ground/hazard checks until release, avoiding the source's potential mid-carry reset. Invalid numerical states recover to a safe point; ordinary slow/stationary balls do not trigger a reset.
   38 | - Aim dots retain the original difficulty-dependent preview: a short direction/friction estimate in three courses and a bounded physics/gravity preview in Event Horizon. The latter uses a disposable simulation snapshot, never mutates the live ball and stops at collisions, portals or hazards. Moving hazards can still change before release.
   39 | - The third source portal exited into the void. Its destination moved from (960,250) to (960,310), so the 35-unit exit offset lands inside the intended platform with ball clearance. No difficult obstacle was removed.
   40 | - Horizon UFO visits begin at 11.5 obstacle seconds and repeat every 28; warning 1.5 s, speed 170, active duration 13 s, hover 1 s, carry 0.8 s, cooldown 8 s. These values live in course data. Seed/event hashing makes independent competitors reproducible.
   41 | - Persistent contact oscillation (8 seconds, under 55 world units, over 24 impacts, still moving) recovers to a safe last shot. Legitimate resting/slow balls do not trigger this detector.
   42 | - Original named-player score files, desktop intro/credits screens and original art/audio are replaced by Pocket Rivals' local records, navigation and procedural effects.
   43 | - The single existing `mini-golf` registry identity now launches this faithful solo port in Arcade. The previous five-course duel source is retained but unregistered, with no duplicate menu card. Old golf duel checkpoints/tournament rounds cannot resume as Ultimate Golf; create a new tournament. Other game saves and scores remain intact. Golf has dedicated AI/local races, separate from the global duel tournament.
   44 | - Course records persist; an interrupted active golf course restarts. Android hardware and iOS Safari still require physical-device verification.
   45 | 
   46 | ## Evidence
   47 | 
   48 | `tests/fixtures/golf-solutions.ts` contains reproducible **legal Easy-mode shots from each original tee to its cup**, without teleporting, bypassing hazards or resetting positions: Foundry 15, Shoreline 15, Event Horizon 13, Lost Temple 11. These replay against the same simulation used in the browser. The optional route-search source in `tests/fixtures/golf-route-search.ts` documents how those fixtures were found; it is not shipped or run by default.
   49 | 
   50 | Additional targeted tests cover collision projection/tunneling, 30/60/120 FPS equivalence, stroke limits, all cup completions, tides, currents, portals, UFO release, bridges, door plates, quicksand, three-difficulty stress, and coordinate inversion. Browser tests exercise real mouse/touch events, cancellation, pause, all courses, zoom, resizing, restarts and disposal. A complete Lost Temple browser run also reaches the cup in 14 strokes through real touch events, then verifies victory, score banking and persistence after reload. See `QA.md` for full-suite results and `performance-report.json` for measured desktop Chrome samples.
   51 | 
   52 | The upstream checkout contains no LICENSE file. No claim of a redistribution license is made; confirm author permission for the mechanically derived port/course layouts before independent commercial publication. Nothing was published or pushed.
   53 | 
   54 | ## Golf modes
   55 | 
   56 | - **Casual** retains all original challenge settings, stroke allowances, points and personal records.
   57 | - **2 Player** is hot-seat: Player 1 completes the selected course/tour, then Player 2 receives identical seeded initial conditions. Each course has a 180-second foreground timeout and Easy stroke allowance. Menus, help, handoffs and pause time are excluded. Completing the tour beats DNF; two DNFs draw. Otherwise total time wins, within 0.1 s fewer strokes wins, then draw.
   58 | - **vs AI** advances two independent physics worlds concurrently. A blue outlined ghost shows the real opponent position when on the same course. The first completed tour wins; a 0.1 s window handles effectively simultaneous finishes. Exceeding time/strokes or forfeiting loses, simultaneous failure draws. Results/rematch are module-owned.
   59 | - Competition counters use `pocket-rivals.golf-versus.v1`, never the casual record key.
   60 | 
   61 | `modes/` isolates clocks/progression/scoring; `ai/` contains navigation waypoints and the shot planner. The planner simulates candidate angles, powers and waiting times against a live physics snapshot in a cancellable worker. Medium/Hard/Impossible use 65/140/240 ms search budgets and 1.1/0.8/0.65 s decision delays; Medium has small periodic aiming errors. AI calls the same `shoot` API and uses the same limits. Impossible is bounded practical search, not optimal play. Waypoints are route guidance, not scripted shot velocities. Performance budgets can reduce candidate count on slower hardware.
   62 | 
   63 | Run `npx vitest run --config tests/fixtures/golf-audit.config.ts` for the optional full AI route audit. The tested seed (123), Impossible difficulty and simulated decision timing completed all four courses legally (15/15/10/13 shots in the recorded run); this is not a guarantee for every seed or difficulty. The normal route fixtures separately establish legal course completion and never alter ball positions. Full browser tests now use responsive DOM controls and verify focused touch input, mouse input, mobile/landscape footer spacing, hot-seat handoff, real worker shots, pause/cleanup, and a complete casual Temple run.
~~~

## docs/specifications/13-games.md
SHA-256: a778c4c77d1db66744d9060d2ad5d6b1a0963e292cfdcf0b484048034f1f9b79
~~~text
    1 | # POCKET RIVALS — GRAND CODEX IMPLEMENTATION PROMPT
    2 | ## 13 New Mini-Games, Advanced Mathematical Challenges, AI Opponents, Sound Effects, Tournaments & Cross-Platform Optimization
    3 | 
    4 | # 1. PROJECT OVERVIEW
    5 | 
    6 | You are working on **Pocket Rivals**, an existing minimalist multiplayer mini-game collection developed using:
    7 | 
    8 | - TypeScript
    9 | - Phaser 3
   10 | - Vite
   11 | - Capacitor for Android
   12 | - The project's existing modular game architecture
   13 | 
   14 | I want you to implement **13 fully functional new mini-games**, inspired by the gameplay concepts demonstrated in my attached 23-page reference PDF.
   15 | 
   16 | The primary reference application is:
   17 | 
   18 | https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.JindoBlu.TwoPlayerGamesChallenge&hl=en
   19 | 
   20 | Study the game design principles of this application, particularly:
   21 | 
   22 | - Instant, easy-to-understand gameplay.
   23 | - Local multiplayer on one device.
   24 | - Responsive touch controls.
   25 | - Short, competitive matches.
   26 | - Simple but polished graphics.
   27 | - AI opponents with multiple difficulties.
   28 | - Consistent score tracking.
   29 | - Fast transitions between games.
   30 | - Replayability.
   31 | 
   32 | The attached PDF provides gameplay references for 13 mini-games.
   33 | 
   34 | **Use the PDF to understand the mechanics, not to duplicate copyrighted graphics, audio, branding, or code.** All new visuals should follow Pocket Rivals' existing original aesthetic.
   35 | 
   36 | ## Fundamental Development Requirement
   37 | 
   38 | **Implement every game ONE BY ONE.**
   39 | 
   40 | Do not create 13 incomplete demonstrations and attempt to finish them afterward.
   41 | 
   42 | The correct process is:
   43 | 
   44 | 1. Understand a game's rules.
   45 | 2. Implement its complete gameplay logic.
   46 | 3. Implement its controls.
   47 | 4. Implement AI.
   48 | 5. Implement scoring and victory conditions.
   49 | 6. Add appropriate sound effects.
   50 | 7. Integrate it into Pocket Rivals.
   51 | 8. Test it thoroughly.
   52 | 9. Fix bugs.
   53 | 10. Move to the next game.
   54 | 
   55 | Each game must be independently playable before another is started.
   56 | 
   57 | ### Priority Order
   58 | 
   59 | 1. Actual runnability and functionality.
   60 | 2. Correct game mechanics.
   61 | 3. Correct scoring and winner detection.
   62 | 4. Smooth, responsive controls.
   63 | 5. Stable AI.
   64 | 6. Cross-platform compatibility.
   65 | 7. Smooth physics and animations.
   66 | 8. Consistent minimalist visuals.
   67 | 9. Performance and scalability.
   68 | 10. Additional polish.
   69 | 
   70 | Never prioritize visual complexity over reliable gameplay.
   71 | 
   72 | ---
   73 | 
   74 | # 2. PRE-IMPLEMENTATION ANALYSIS
   75 | 
   76 | Before modifying the codebase:
   77 | 
   78 | 1. Read the root AGENTS.md.
   79 | 2. Inspect the existing source structure.
   80 | 3. Identify all registered mini-games.
   81 | 4. Understand the GameRegistry and GameLoader.
   82 | 5. Inspect the current AI implementations.
   83 | 6. Inspect the scoring and tournament systems.
   84 | 7. Inspect the touch/mouse input architecture.
   85 | 8. Inspect existing scene-transition code.
   86 | 9. Inspect existing audio infrastructure.
   87 | 10. Inspect the responsive layout system.
   88 | 11. Review the attached rules PDF.
   89 | 12. Identify overlapping or duplicated gameplay modules.
   90 | 
   91 | Do not replace working functionality unnecessarily.
   92 | 
   93 | If the repository differs from the assumed architecture, adapt your implementation to the actual code.
   94 | 
   95 | Preserve the current Pocket Rivals design system, especially:
   96 | 
   97 | - Warm off-white backgrounds.
   98 | - Orange and blue player identities.
   99 | - Pastel-colored playing surfaces.
  100 | - Thick dark outlines.
  101 | - Rounded cards and buttons.
  102 | - Minimalist vector illustrations.
  103 | - Clear typography.
  104 | - Smooth and restrained animations.
  105 | 
  106 | The new games must feel like original Pocket Rivals titles, not imported applications.
  107 | 
  108 | ---
  109 | 
  110 | # 3. GAMES TO IMPLEMENT
  111 | 
  112 | Implement these 13 games:
  113 | 
  114 | 1. Car Duel
  115 | 2. Archery Duel
  116 | 3. Gravity Runner
  117 | 4. Light Fingers
  118 | 5. Fruit Duel
  119 | 6. Happy Birds
  120 | 7. Math Quiz
  121 | 8. Dots and Boxes
  122 | 9. Lumberjack
  123 | 10. Hammer Hit
  124 | 11. Flappy Jump
  125 | 12. Chicken Jump
  126 | 13. Spike Attacks
  127 | 
  128 | Every game must support:
  129 | 
  130 | - Local two-player mode.
  131 | - Single-player versus AI.
  132 | - Medium AI.
  133 | - Hard AI.
  134 | - Impossible AI.
  135 | - How to Play instructions.
  136 | - Pause and resume.
  137 | - Restart and rematch.
  138 | - Sound effects.
  139 | - Correct winner detection.
  140 | - Existing tournament integration.
  141 | - Mobile touch controls.
  142 | - Desktop mouse or keyboard controls.
  143 | 
  144 | The rules below combine the PDF's explicit mechanics with agreed implementation defaults where the PDF is incomplete. Preserve these defaults for now, but document them as configurable design decisions rather than claiming they are confirmed original-game rules.
  145 | 
  146 | ---
  147 | 
  148 | # 4. DETAILED GAME SPECIFICATIONS
  149 | 
  150 | ## GAME 01 — CAR DUEL
  151 | 
  152 | Reference: PDF pages 1–3.
  153 | 
  154 | ### Gameplay Concept
  155 | 
  156 | A 2D side-view vehicle battle where players attempt to strike their opponent's driver's head without exposing their own.
  157 | 
  158 | Two cars spawn on opposite sides of an arena.
  159 | 
  160 | The cars use simple but stable physics involving acceleration, momentum, rotations, wheel contact, and collisions.
  161 | 
  162 | ### Rules
  163 | 
  164 | - Each player controls forward and backward movement.
  165 | - Vehicles can collide, tilt, roll, and flip.
  166 | - Every driver has a clearly defined head hitbox.
  167 | - If the driver's head collides with a dangerous surface or object, that driver loses the round.
  168 | - The opponent receives one point for the round.
  169 | - If both drivers lose simultaneously, replay the round.
  170 | - First player to win 5 rounds wins the match.
  171 | 
  172 | ### Controls
  173 | 
  174 | Mobile:
  175 | - Left side of screen: Player 1 controls.
  176 | - Right side: Player 2 controls.
  177 | - Two directional buttons per player.
  178 | 
  179 | Desktop:
  180 | - Player 1: A/D.
  181 | - Player 2: Left/Right arrows.
  182 | 
  183 | Support simultaneous inputs.
  184 | 
  185 | ### Physics Requirements
  186 | 
  187 | Implement:
  188 | 
  189 | - Predictable vehicle acceleration.
  190 | - Gradual braking and momentum.
  191 | - Gravity.
  192 | - Body rotation.
  193 | - Wheel-ground contact.
  194 | - Collision impulses.
  195 | - Head-specific collision detection.
  196 | - Stable terrain collision.
  197 | 
  198 | Avoid unstable flipping, perpetual vibration, penetration through walls, and impossible recoveries.
  199 | 
  200 | ### AI
  201 | 
  202 | **Medium:** Basic movement and occasional poor decisions.
  203 | 
  204 | **Hard:** Predicts collisions, protects its own head, and attempts deliberate attacks.
  205 | 
  206 | **Impossible:** Strong maneuver planning and precise control without violating physical limitations.
  207 | 
  208 | ### Audio
  209 | 
  210 | - Short engine acceleration.
  211 | - Tire skid.
  212 | - Vehicle collision.
  213 | - Metallic impact.
  214 | - Driver-hit impact.
  215 | - Round victory.
  216 | 
  217 | No continuous background soundtrack.
  218 | 
  219 | ---
  220 | 
  221 | ## GAME 02 — ARCHERY DUEL
  222 | 
  223 | Reference: PDF pages 4–10.
  224 | 
  225 | ### Gameplay Concept
  226 | 
  227 | A competitive shooting game based on carefully timed inputs.
  228 | 
  229 | Players must lock horizontal and vertical aiming positions before shooting.
  230 | 
  231 | ### Rules
  232 | 
  233 | Each shooting attempt has three steps:
  234 | 
  235 | 1. First tap begins horizontal crosshair movement.
  236 | 2. Second tap locks the horizontal position and begins vertical crosshair movement.
  237 | 3. Third tap locks vertical positioning and fires.
  238 | 
  239 | The projectile travels toward the chosen position.
  240 | 
  241 | ### Scoring
  242 | 
  243 | - Hit a large target: 1 point.
  244 | - Hit a small target: 2 points.
  245 | - Miss: 0 points.
  246 | - First player to 10 points wins.
  247 | 
  248 | ### Important Details
  249 | 
  250 | - Target sizes must match their collision boundaries.
  251 | - Small targets should be meaningfully harder.
  252 | - Crosshair motion must be consistent and smooth.
  253 | - Rapid tapping must not accidentally skip states.
  254 | - Each attempt should reset cleanly.
  255 | - Targets should vary positions to maintain replayability.
  256 | 
  257 | ### AI
  258 | 
  259 | Medium: Slow or imprecise timing.
  260 | 
  261 | Hard: Accurate target locking.
  262 | 
  263 | Impossible: Near-perfect timing with legal reaction behavior.
  264 | 
  265 | ### Audio
  266 | 
  267 | - Aiming lock.
  268 | - Bowstring release.
  269 | - Arrow flight.
  270 | - Target impact.
  271 | - Successful scoring.
  272 | 
  273 | ---
  274 | 
  275 | ## GAME 03 — GRAVITY RUNNER
  276 | 
  277 | Reference: PDF pages 11–13.
  278 | 
  279 | ### Gameplay Concept
  280 | 
  281 | Two runners move automatically through an endless side-scrolling obstacle course.
  282 | 
  283 | A tap reverses gravity, moving the character between floor and ceiling.
  284 | 
  285 | ### Rules
  286 | 
  287 | - Characters move automatically.
  288 | - Players tap to reverse gravity.
  289 | - Avoid gaps in the floor and ceiling.
  290 | - Falling into a gap loses the round.
  291 | - Speed increases with survival duration.
  292 | - The last surviving player wins the round.
  293 | - First player to win 5 rounds wins.
  294 | 
  295 | If both fail in the same simulation step, replay the round.
  296 | 
  297 | ### Course Generation
  298 | 
  299 | Procedurally generate valid floor/ceiling patterns.
  300 | 
  301 | Ensure every obstacle sequence has at least one physically possible survival route.
  302 | 
  303 | Do not create unavoidable deaths.
  304 | 
  305 | Use a shared random seed for both players so difficulty is comparable.
  306 | 
  307 | ### AI
  308 | 
  309 | Medium: Reactive gravity switching.
  310 | 
  311 | Hard: Predictive obstacle avoidance.
  312 | 
  313 | Impossible: Strong path planning and precise gravity-switch timing.
  314 | 
  315 | ### Audio
  316 | 
  317 | - Gravity reversal.
  318 | - Landing.
  319 | - Air movement.
  320 | - Collision.
  321 | - Failure and victory.
  322 | 
  323 | ---
  324 | 
  325 | ## GAME 04 — LIGHT FINGERS
  326 | 
  327 | Reference: PDF page 14.
  328 | 
  329 | ### Gameplay Concept
  330 | 
  331 | A quick-reaction contest in which players compete to grab a diamond.
  332 | 
  333 | ### Rules
  334 | 
  335 | - Both players wait for a random signal.
  336 | - A diamond becomes claimable.
  337 | - The first valid tap wins the round.
  338 | - Tapping before the signal is a false start.
  339 | - A false start awards the opponent one round victory.
  340 | - First player to win 5 rounds wins.
  341 | 
  342 | ### Fairness
  343 | 
  344 | - Use the same activation event for both players.
  345 | - Handle simultaneous taps deterministically.
  346 | - Avoid predictable signal intervals.
  347 | - Make the signal clearly visible before accepting valid claims.
  348 | - Prevent multi-touch or repeated-event exploits.
  349 | 
  350 | ### AI
  351 | 
  352 | Medium: Noticeable human-like reaction delay.
  353 | 
  354 | Hard: Faster reaction.
  355 | 
  356 | Impossible: Extremely quick but not instantaneous or preemptive.
  357 | 
  358 | ### Audio
  359 | 
  360 | - Signal activation.
  361 | - Diamond collection.
  362 | - False-start buzzer.
  363 | - Round victory.
  364 | 
  365 | ---
  366 | 
  367 | ## GAME 05 — FRUIT DUEL
  368 | 
  369 | Reference: PDF page 15.
  370 | 
  371 | ### Gameplay Concept
  372 | 
  373 | A fast-paced reaction game requiring recognition of fruit icons.
  374 | 
  375 | ### Rules
  376 | 
  377 | - Display a target fruit at the start of each round.
  378 | - Show a sequence of fruit icons.
  379 | - Players must tap when the displayed fruit matches the target.
  380 | - Correct first response earns 1 point.
  381 | - Incorrect response awards 1 point to the opponent.

  469 | 
  470 | # GAME 07 — MATH QUIZ
  471 | 
  472 | ## One of the Most Important New Games
  473 | 
  474 | Reference: PDF page 17.
  475 | 
  476 | This game is intended to support fast-paced mathematics competitions between friends.
  477 | 
  478 | It must have two clearly separated categories:
  479 | 
  480 | 1. **Basic Arithmetic**
  481 | 2. **University Math Challenge**
  482 | 
  483 | The second category must contain clever questions suitable for BUET undergraduate students but still solvable entirely in the head.
  484 | 
  485 | Do not confuse advanced mathematics with lengthy calculations.
  486 | 
  487 | ## 7.1 Core Gameplay Rules
  488 | 
  489 | Both players are shown the same mathematical question.
  490 | 
  491 | Every question has exactly **three multiple-choice options**.
  492 | 
  493 | Only one option is correct.
  494 | 
  495 | Scoring:
  496 | 
  497 | - First correct answer earns 1 point.
  498 | - An incorrect answer awards 1 point to the opponent.
  499 | - The question ends as soon as a valid scoring event occurs.
  500 | - First player to 10 points wins.
  501 | 
  502 | Make sure each question is resolved only once.
  503 | 
  504 | Prevent double scoring caused by rapid taps.
  505 | 
  506 | ### Local Multiplayer Presentation
  507 | 
  508 | Split the screen into two clearly separated response areas.
  509 | 
  510 | Both players should be able to read the same question comfortably.
  511 | 
  512 | Each player must have three large answer buttons.
  513 | 
  514 | The layout can be mirrored or rotated where necessary so players sitting at opposite ends of a smartphone can answer comfortably.
  515 | 
  516 | Questions must remain legible on small screens.
  517 | 
  518 | ### AI
  519 | 
  520 | Medium:
  521 | - Longer simulated reasoning time.
  522 | - Occasional incorrect answers.
  523 | 
  524 | Hard:
  525 | - Faster and more accurate.
  526 | 
  527 | Impossible:
  528 | - Very high answer accuracy and fast response time, but no responses before the question is displayed.
  529 | 
  530 | AI should not require external APIs.
  531 | 
  532 | For banked questions, use the validated correct answer plus calibrated response timing. Do not misrepresent this as a general-purpose symbolic reasoning engine.
  533 | 
  534 | ---
  535 | 
  536 | ## 7.2 CATEGORY A — BASIC ARITHMETIC
  537 | 
  538 | This is the casual category.
  539 | 
  540 | Topics:
  541 | 
  542 | - Addition.
  543 | - Subtraction.
  544 | - Multiplication.
  545 | - Division.
  546 | - Operator precedence.
  547 | - Simple fractions.
  548 | - Basic percentage calculations.

  558 | \]

  561 | 
  562 | B. \(96\)

  577 | 
  578 | B. \(13\)
  579 |

  587 |

  590 | \]

  608 | ## 7.3 CATEGORY B — UNIVERSITY MATH CHALLENGE
  609 | 
  610 | ### Target Audience
  611 | 
  612 | Students comfortable with advanced HSC mathematics and introductory university-level mathematics, including BUET undergraduate students.
  613 | 
  614 | ### Core Philosophy
  615 | 
  616 | **Conceptually tricky but mentally solvable.**
  617 | 
  618 | Every question should be answerable within approximately 10–30 seconds by a reasonably prepared student.
  619 | 
  620 | No notebook.
  621 | 
  622 | No rough paper.
  623 | 
  624 | No calculator.
  625 | 
  626 | No extensive symbolic manipulation.
  627 |

  629 |

  631 | - Familiarity with standard derivatives.
  632 | - Understanding of integration properties.

  639 |

  641 |

  651 | - Simple Taylor-series concepts.
  652 |

  654 |

  684 |

  686 |

  689 | - Diagonalization.

  706 | 
  707 | ## 7.4 UNIVERSITY MATH — EXAMPLE QUESTIONS
  708 | 
  709 | All examples below use LaTeX notation.
  710 | 
  711 | Store mathematical expressions as valid LaTeX strings in the question bank.
  712 | 
  713 | ### Example 1 — Differentiation
  714 | 
  715 | Given
  716 | 
  717 | \[
  718 | f(x)=x^x,
  719 | \]
  720 | 
  721 | find
  722 | 
  723 | \[
  724 | f'(1).
  725 | \]
  726 | 
  727 | Options:
  728 | 
  729 | A. \(0\)
  730 | 
  731 | B. \(1\)
  732 | 
  733 | C. \(e\)
  734 | 
  735 | **Correct: B**
  736 | 
  737 | Reason:
  738 | 
  739 | \[
  740 | \frac{d}{dx}x^x=x^x(\ln x+1),
  741 | \]
  742 | 
  743 | so
  744 | 
  745 | \[
  746 | f'(1)=1.
  747 | \]
  748 | 
  749 | The player should recognize or mentally recall the logarithmic differentiation result.
  750 | 
  751 | ### Example 2 — Definite Integration
  752 | 
  753 | Evaluate
  754 | 
  755 | \[
  756 | \int_0^\pi \sin x\,dx.
  757 | \]
  758 | 
  759 | Options:
  760 | 
  761 | A. \(0\)
  762 | 
  763 | B. \(1\)
  764 | 
  765 | C. \(2\)
  766 | 
  767 | **Correct: C**
  768 | 
  769 | Mental observation:
  770 | 
  771 | \[
  772 | [-\cos x]_0^\pi=2.
  773 | \]
  774 | 
  775 | ### Example 3 — Standard Limit
  776 | 
  777 | Evaluate
  778 | 
  779 | \[
  780 | \lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin 3x}{x}.
  781 | \]
  782 | 
  783 | Options:
  784 | 
  785 | A. \(1\)
  786 | 
  787 | B. \(3\)
  788 | 
  789 | C. \(0\)
  790 | 
  791 | **Correct: B**
  792 | 
  793 | Use
  794 | 
  795 | \[
  796 | \lim_{u\to0}\frac{\sin u}{u}=1.
  797 | \]
  798 | 
  799 | ### Example 4 — Matrix Determinant
  800 | 
  801 | If \(A\) is a \(2\times2\) matrix and
  802 | 
  803 | \[
  804 | \det(A)=3,
  805 | \]
  806 | 
  807 | find
  808 | 
  809 | \[
  810 | \det(2A).
  811 | \]
  812 | 
  813 | Options:
  814 | 
  815 | A. \(6\)
  816 | 
  817 | B. \(12\)
  818 | 
  819 | C. \(9\)
  820 | 
  821 | **Correct: B**
  822 | 
  823 | Because
  824 | 
  825 | \[
  826 | \det(kA)=k^n\det(A)
  827 | \]
  828 | 
  829 | for an \(n\times n\) matrix, so
  830 | 
  831 | \[
  832 | \det(2A)=2^2\cdot3=12.
  833 | \]
  834 | 
  835 | ### Example 5 — Complex Numbers
  836 | 
  837 | Evaluate
  838 | 
  839 | \[
  840 | i^{2026}.
  841 | \]
  842 | 
  843 | Options:
  844 | 
  845 | A. \(1\)
  846 | 
  847 | B. \(-1\)
  848 | 
  849 | C. \(i\)
  850 | 
  851 | **Correct: B**
  852 | 
  853 | Since powers of \(i\) repeat every four.
  854 | 
  855 | ### Example 6 — Odd Function Trick
  856 | 
  857 | Evaluate
  858 | 
  859 | \[
  860 | \int_{-1}^{1}x^5\cos x\,dx.
  861 | \]
  862 | 
  863 | Options:
  864 | 
  865 | A. \(0\)
  866 | 
  867 | B. \(1\)
  868 | 
  869 | C. \(-1\)
  870 | 
  871 | **Correct: A**
  872 | 
  873 | The integrand is odd, so the integral vanishes over symmetric limits.
  874 | 
  875 | This is an excellent example of a tricky but mentally solvable question.
  876 | 
  877 | ### Example 7 — Exponential Limit
  878 | 
  879 | Evaluate
  880 | 
  881 | \[
  882 | \lim_{x\to0}\frac{e^{2x}-1}{x}.
  883 | \]
  884 | 
  885 | Options:
  886 | 
  887 | A. \(1\)
  888 | 
  889 | B. \(2\)
  890 | 
  891 | C. \(e^2\)
  892 | 
  893 | **Correct: B**
  894 | 
  895 | ### Example 8 — Trigonometric Derivative
  896 | 
  897 | Evaluate
  898 | 
  899 | \[
  900 | \left.\frac{d}{dx}\sin^2x\right|_{x=\pi/4}.
  901 | \]
  902 | 
  903 | Options:
  904 | 
  905 | A. \(0\)
  906 | 
  907 | B. \(1\)
  908 | 
  909 | C. \(2\)
  910 | 
  911 | **Correct: B**
  912 | 
  913 | Use
  914 | 
  915 | \[
  916 | \frac{d}{dx}\sin^2x=\sin2x.
  917 | \]
  918 | 
  919 | ### Example 9 — Infinite Series
  920 | 
  921 | Evaluate
  922 | 
  923 | \[
  924 | \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{2^n}.
  925 | \]
  926 | 
  927 | Options:
  928 | 
  929 | A. \(\frac12\)
  930 | 
  931 | B. \(1\)
  932 | 
  933 | C. \(2\)
  934 | 
  935 | **Correct: B**
  936 | 
  937 | ### Example 10 — Probability
  938 | 
  939 | A fair coin is tossed twice.
  940 | 
  941 | What is the probability of getting at least one head?
  942 | 
  943 | A. \(\frac12\)
  944 | 
  945 | B. \(\frac34\)
  946 | 
  947 | C. \(\frac14\)
  948 | 
  949 | **Correct: B**
  950 | 
  951 | Use the complement:
  952 | 
  953 | \[
  954 | P(\text{at least one head})
  955 | =1-P(\text{no heads})
  956 | =1-\frac14
  957 | =\frac34.
  958 | \]
  959 | 
  960 | These examples establish the desired question style.
  961 | 
  962 | Generate additional problems of comparable or moderately greater conceptual difficulty.
  963 | 
  964 | ---
  965 | 
  966 | ## 7.5 QUESTION BANK REQUIREMENTS
  967 | 
  968 | Create at least **100 rigorously verified University Math Challenge questions**.
  969 | 
  970 | Each question must contain:
  971 | 
  972 | - Unique ID.
  973 | - Topic.
  974 | - Difficulty.
  975 | - LaTeX question statement.
  976 | - Exactly three LaTeX-compatible answer options.
  977 | - Correct answer index.
  978 | - Concise mathematical explanation.
  979 | - Estimated mental-solving time.
  980 | 
  981 | Suggested question-bank format:
  982 | 
  983 | ```ts
  984 | type MathQuestion = {
  985 |   id: string;
  986 |   topic: string;
  987 |   difficulty: "easy" | "medium" | "hard";
  988 |   questionLatex: string;
  989 |   optionsLatex: [string, string, string];
  990 |   correctIndex: 0 | 1 | 2;
  991 |   explanationLatex: string;
  992 |   estimatedSeconds: number;
  993 | };
  994 | ```
  995 | 
  996 | Do not embed mathematical expressions in raw HTML.
  997 | 
  998 | Use a math renderer such as KaTeX.
  999 | 
 1000 | Ensure LaTeX backslashes are preserved correctly in TypeScript strings, preferably through `String.raw` template literals or properly escaped strings.
 1001 | 
 1002 | Do not create malformed LaTeX.
 1003 | 
 1004 | ### Internal Difficulty Categories
 1005 | 
 1006 | **Easy — 5–10 seconds**
 1007 | 
 1008 | Immediate recognition of a standard identity or formula.
 1009 | 
 1010 | **Medium — 10–20 seconds**
 1011 | 
 1012 | One or two mental steps.
 1013 | 
 1014 | **Hard — 20–30 seconds**
 1015 | 
 1016 | A clever property, conceptual trap, or deeper observation.
 1017 | 
 1018 | Even Hard questions must require no written calculation.
 1019 | 
 1020 | ### Validation
 1021 | 
 1022 | Before adding a question to the production bank, verify:
 1023 | 
 1024 | 1. The mathematical expression is valid.
 1025 | 2. The question has exactly one correct answer.
 1026 | 3. The answer key is correct.
 1027 | 4. Distractors are mathematically distinct from the correct answer and one another.
 1028 | 5. No options are equivalent under algebraic simplification.
 1029 | 6. Any required assumptions or domains are specified.
 1030 | 7. The question is realistically solvable mentally.
 1031 | 8. The rendered expression fits on a mobile display.
 1032 | 
 1033 | Where possible, use development-time symbolic or numerical checks.
 1034 | 
 1035 | For questions that cannot be reliably verified automatically, mark them for manual mathematical review.
 1036 | 
 1037 | Do not falsely claim independent verification if the questions were only generated and never checked.
 1038 | 
 1039 | ### Question Randomization
 1040 | 
 1041 | - Randomize question order.
 1042 | - Avoid immediate repetition.
 1043 | - Balance topics.
 1044 | - Randomize answer positions.
 1045 | - Avoid predictable correct-option patterns.
 1046 | - Preserve mathematically valid answer mappings after shuffling.
 1047 | 
 1048 | ### Math Rendering
 1049 | 
 1050 | Use a lightweight, lazy-loaded LaTeX renderer.
 1051 | 
 1052 | Support:
 1053 | 
 1054 | \[
 1055 | \int_a^b f(x)\,dx
 1056 | \]
 1057 | 
 1058 | \[
 1059 | \lim_{x\to a}f(x)
 1060 | \]
 1061 | 
 1062 | \[
 1063 | \frac{dy}{dx}
 1064 | \]
 1065 | 
 1066 | \[
 1067 | \sum_{k=1}^{n}k
 1068 | \]
 1069 | 
 1070 | \[
 1071 | \begin{pmatrix}
 1072 | a&b\\
 1073 | c&d
 1074 | \end{pmatrix}
 1075 | \]
 1076 | 
 1077 | Render formulas sharply at different screen resolutions.
 1078 | 
 1079 | Do not use screenshots of mathematical expressions.
 1080 | 
 1081 | The quiz must be playable in both browsers and Capacitor Android.
 1082 |

 1169 | ## GAME 10 — HAMMER HIT
 1170 | 
 1171 | Reference: PDF page 20.
 1172 | 
 1173 | ### Gameplay
 1174 | 
 1175 | A needle oscillates across a timing gauge.
 1176 | 
 1177 | Players must tap when the needle approaches the ideal strike position.
 1178 | 
 1179 | ### Rules
 1180 | 
 1181 | - Each player gets exactly three attempts.
 1182 | - Tapping locks the timing needle.
 1183 | - Accuracy determines strike power and score.
 1184 | - The closer the needle is to the ideal position, the higher the score.
 1185 | - The final result uses the **arithmetic mean of all three attempts**.
 1186 | - Highest average wins.
 1187 | 
 1188 | ### Critical Mathematical Requirement
 1189 | 
 1190 | For attempt scores \(S_1,S_2,S_3\),
 1191 | 
 1192 | \[
 1193 | \boxed{\bar S=\frac{S_1+S_2+S_3}{3}}
 1194 | \]
 1195 | 
 1196 | Use this formula.
 1197 | 
 1198 | **Do not use the highest attempt.**
 1199 | 
 1200 | ### Example
 1201 | 
 1202 | Player 1:
 1203 | 
 1204 | \[
 1205 | S_1=80,\quad S_2=60,\quad S_3=100
 1206 | \]
 1207 | 
 1208 | \[
 1209 | \bar S_1=\frac{80+60+100}{3}=80
 1210 | \]
 1211 | 
 1212 | Player 2:
 1213 | 
 1214 | \[
 1215 | S_1=75,\quad S_2=90,\quad S_3=90
 1216 | \]
 1217 | 
 1218 | \[
 1219 | \bar S_2=\frac{75+90+90}{3}=85
 1220 | \]
 1221 | 
 1222 | Player 2 wins.
 1223 | 
 1224 | ### Numerical Accuracy
 1225 | 
 1226 | Use exact integer totals internally when scores are integers.
 1227 | 
 1228 | Do not round averages before comparing winners.
 1229 | 
 1230 | Only round for display.
 1231 | 
 1232 | Equal averages produce a draw in Quick Play.
 1233 | 
 1234 | ### AI
 1235 | 
 1236 | Medium: Imprecise timing.
 1237 | 
 1238 | Hard: Good accuracy.
 1239 | 
 1240 | Impossible: Near-perfect legal timing.
 1241 | 
 1242 | ### Audio
 1243 | 
 1244 | - Hammer swing.
 1245 | - Metal impact.
 1246 | - Heavy strike.
 1247 | - Perfect-hit effect.
 1248 | - Score reveal.
 1249 | 
 1250 | Vary the impact sound according to strike strength.

 1302 | 
 1303 | ## GAME 12 — CHICKEN JUMP
 1304 | 
 1305 | Reference: PDF page 22.
 1306 | 
 1307 | ### Concept
 1308 | 
 1309 | A block-stacking game involving timing and landing accuracy.
 1310 | 
 1311 | ### Rules
 1312 | 
 1313 | - A chicken jumps upward.
 1314 | - A block moves horizontally beneath it.
 1315 | - Players tap to stop the moving block.
 1316 | - The chicken must land on the block.
 1317 | - A successful landing scores one point.
 1318 | - The stack grows with successful attempts.
 1319 | - Missing the block fails the attempt.
 1320 | - First to 10 successful stacks wins.
 1321 | 
 1322 | ### Physics and Fairness
 1323 | 
 1324 | - Determine collisions geometrically.
 1325 | - Allow small realistic alignment tolerance.
 1326 | - Gradually increase difficulty.
 1327 | - Avoid impossible block speeds.
 1328 | - Prevent overlapping or invalid block states.
 1329 | 
 1330 | ### AI
 1331 | 
 1332 | Medium: Moderate timing errors.
 1333 | 
 1334 | Hard: Accurate alignment.
 1335 | 
 1336 | Impossible: Very precise placement.
 1337 | 
 1338 | ### Sound
 1339 | 
 1340 | - Jump.
 1341 | - Block sliding.
 1342 | - Block lock.
 1343 | - Landing.
 1344 | - Failure.
 1345 | - Victory.

 1349 | ## GAME 13 — SPIKE ATTACKS
 1350 | 
 1351 | Reference: PDF page 23.

 1353 | ### Concept
 1354 | 
 1355 | A survival game where players hide behind stones to avoid incoming spikes.
 1356 | 
 1357 | ### Rules
 1358 | 
 1359 | - Spikes arrive in waves.
 1360 | - Players can move around a constrained arena.
 1361 | - Stones provide protection.
 1362 | - Direct spike hits cause round loss.
 1363 | - Last survivor wins the round.
 1364 | - First player to win 5 rounds wins.
 1365 |

 1367 | 
 1368 | - Stone collision must be reliable.
 1369 | - Spikes should collide with protective obstacles before reaching players.
 1370 | - Show warning cues for dangerous attacks.
 1371 | - Generate fair survival patterns.
 1372 | - Avoid unavoidable spike configurations.
 1373 |

 1375 | 
 1376 | Medium: Basic cover selection.
 1377 | 
 1378 | Hard: Predictive safe-position selection.
 1379 | 
 1380 | Impossible: Advanced threat avoidance.

 1392 | # 5. GLOBAL AI SYSTEM

 1394 | Every new game must support the existing Pocket Rivals AI difficulty selection.

 1399 | - Reasonable mistakes.

    4 | import { rounded, label } from "../../shared/components/drawing";
    5 | class TapDuel implements MiniGame {
    6 |   private score: [number, number] = [0, 0];
    7 |   private paused = false;
    8 |   private finished = false;
    9 |   private graphics!: Phaser.GameObjects.Graphics;
   10 |   private labels: Phaser.GameObjects.Text[] = [];
   11 |   initialize(ctx: GameContext) {
   12 |     ctx.setHint("TAP YOUR HALF · FIRST TO 10");
   13 |     ctx.setScore(0, 0);
   14 |     this.graphics = ctx.scene.add.graphics();
   15 |     rounded(this.graphics, 24, 112, 372, 260, 22, theme.blue);
   16 |     rounded(this.graphics, 24, 390, 372, 260, 22, theme.orange);
   17 |     this.labels = [
   18 |       label(ctx.scene, 210, 510, "TAP!", 34),
   19 |       label(ctx.scene, 210, 250, "TAP!", 34).setRotation(Math.PI),
   20 |     ];
   21 |     ctx.input.tap((x, y, player) => {
   22 |       if (
   23 |         this.paused ||
   24 |         this.finished ||
   25 |         x < FIELD.left ||
   26 |         x > FIELD.right ||
   27 |         y < FIELD.top ||
   28 |         y > FIELD.bottom
   29 |       )
   30 |         return;
   31 |       this.score[player - 1]++;
   32 |       ctx.setScore(...this.score);
   33 |       ctx.audio.play("hit");
   34 |       if (this.score[player - 1] === 10) {
   35 |         this.finished = true;
   36 |         ctx.finish({ winner: player, scores: [...this.score] });
   37 |       }
   38 |     });
   39 |   }
   40 |   update(_dt: number) {}
   41 |   pause() {
   42 |     this.paused = true;
   43 |   }
   44 |   resume() {
   45 |     this.paused = false;
   46 |   }
   47 |   dispose() {
   48 |     this.graphics.destroy();
   49 |     this.labels.forEach((text) => text.destroy());
   50 |   }
   51 | }
   52 | export default () => new TapDuel();
~~~

## scripts/bundle-report.mjs
SHA-256: 45045c8e76659c9e9c9669ec3766a9587aae22ea1a4f266eafb44a21cd93dfc9
~~~text
    1 | import { readFile, writeFile, readdir } from "node:fs/promises";
    2 | import { gzipSync } from "node:zlib";
    3 | const manifest = JSON.parse(await readFile("dist/.vite/manifest.json", "utf8")),
    4 |   initial = new Set();
    5 | function visit(key) {
    6 |   if (initial.has(key)) return;
    7 |   initial.add(key);
    8 |   for (const child of manifest[key].imports ?? []) visit(child);
    9 | }
   10 | for (const [key, chunk] of Object.entries(manifest))
   11 |   if (chunk.isEntry) visit(key);
   12 | const rows = [];
   13 | for (const key of initial) {
   14 |   const chunk = manifest[key],
   15 |     code = await readFile("dist/" + chunk.file);
   16 |   rows.push({
   17 |     module: key,
   18 |     file: chunk.file,
   19 |     bytes: code.length,
   20 |     gzip: gzipSync(code).length,
   21 |   });
   22 | }
   23 | const gameChunks = Object.keys(manifest).filter((k) =>
   24 |   /src\/(games|arcade)\/.+\/index\.ts$/.test(k),
   25 | );
   26 | if (gameChunks.some((k) => initial.has(k)))
   27 |   throw Error("A game implementation leaked into the initial payload");
   28 | const registered = [];
   29 | for (const root of ["games", "arcade"])
   30 |   for (const folder of await readdir("src/" + root, { withFileTypes: true }))
   31 |     if (folder.isDirectory()) {
   32 |       const files = await readdir("src/" + root + "/" + folder.name);
   33 |       if (files.includes("config.ts") && files.includes("index.ts"))
   34 |         registered.push("src/" + root + "/" + folder.name + "/index.ts");
   35 |     }
   36 | if (registered.some((k) => !gameChunks.includes(k)))
   37 |   throw Error("A registered game is missing its lazy chunk");
   38 | const app = rows.find((r) => r.module === "index.html");
   39 | if (!app || app.gzip > 24000)
   40 |   throw Error(
   41 |     "Application shell exceeded its 24KB gzip budget; inspect imports",
   42 |   );
   43 | const report = {
   44 |   initial: rows,
   45 |   lazyGames: gameChunks,
   46 |   totalInitialGzip: rows.reduce((s, r) => s + r.gzip, 0),
   47 | };
   48 | await writeFile(
   49 |   "docs/bundle-report.json",
   50 |   JSON.stringify(report, null, 2) + "\n",
   51 | );
   52 | console.log(JSON.stringify(report, null, 2));
~~~

## scripts/check-module.mjs
SHA-256: 316820584c20c7a89701327465e0f198fe2fd5dcd5581e8a2ea3dc8e024d8c45
~~~text
    1 | import {
    2 |   realpath,
    3 |   mkdtemp,
    4 |   cp,
    5 |   symlink,
    6 |   readFile,
    7 |   readdir,
    8 |   rm,
    9 | } from "node:fs/promises";
   10 | import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
   11 | import path from "node:path";
   12 | import { build } from "vite";
   13 | import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
   14 | const root = process.cwd(),
   15 |   temp = await realpath(
   16 |     await mkdtemp(path.join(tmpdir(), "pocket-module-check-")),
   17 |   );
   18 | try {
   19 |   for (const p of ["src", "public", "index.html", "tsconfig.json"])
   20 |     await cp(path.join(root, p), path.join(temp, p), { recursive: true });
   21 |   await cp(
   22 |     path.join(root, "examples/tap-duel"),
   23 |     path.join(temp, "src/games/tap-duel"),
   24 |     { recursive: true },
   25 |   );
   26 |   await symlink(
   27 |     path.join(root, "node_modules"),
   28 |     path.join(temp, "node_modules"),
   29 |     "dir",
   30 |   );
   31 |   const check = spawnSync(
   32 |     process.execPath,
   33 |     [
   34 |       path.join(root, "node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc"),
   35 |       "--noEmit",
   36 |       "--project",
   37 |       path.join(temp, "tsconfig.json"),
   38 |     ],
   39 |     { encoding: "utf8" },
   40 |   );
   41 |   if (check.status !== 0) throw Error(check.stdout + check.stderr);
   42 |   await build({
   43 |     root: temp,
   44 |     configFile: false,
   45 |     logLevel: "error",
   46 |     build: { target: "es2022" },
   47 |   });
   48 |   const assets = await readdir(path.join(temp, "dist/assets"));
   49 |   let code = "";
   50 |   for (const file of assets.filter((x) => x.endsWith(".js")))
   51 |     code += await readFile(path.join(temp, "dist/assets", file), "utf8");
   52 |   for (const needle of ["Tap Duel", "tap-duel", "TAP YOUR HALF"])
   53 |     if (!code.includes(needle))
   54 |       throw Error(`Missing discovered module: ${needle}`);
   55 |   console.log(
   56 |     "PASS: copied only a game folder; metadata and lazy implementation compiled automatically. Existing source unchanged.",
   57 |   );
   58 | } finally {
   59 |   await rm(temp, { recursive: true, force: true });
   60 | }

    1 | /** Run against a development server; never enables production telemetry. */
    2 | import { chromium } from "@playwright/test";
    3 | import { writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
    4 | 
    5 | const url = process.env.POCKET_QA_URL ?? "http://127.0.0.1:5173";
    6 | const browser = await chromium.launch({ channel: "chrome", headless: true });
    7 | const results = [];
    8 | try {
    9 |   const page = await browser.newPage({
   10 |     viewport: { width: 412, height: 915 },
   11 |     isMobile: true,
   12 |     hasTouch: true,
   13 |     deviceScaleFactor: 1,
   14 |   });
   15 |   const errors = [];
   16 |   page.on("pageerror", (e) => errors.push(e.message));
   17 |   await page.goto(`${url}/?diagnostics&aiSeed=77`);
   18 |   for (const name of [
   19 |     "Gravity Runner",
   20 |     "Happy Birds",
   21 |     "Spike Attacks",
   22 |   ]) {
   23 |     await page
   24 |       .getByRole("button", { name: `Play ${name}`, exact: true })
   25 |       .click();
   26 |     await page.getByRole("radio", { name: /1 Player/ }).click();
   27 |     await page.getByRole("radio", { name: "Impossible", exact: true }).click();
   28 |     await page.getByRole("button", { name: /Let’s play/ }).click();
   29 |     await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__POCKET__?.scene.ready);
   30 |     await page.waitForTimeout(700);
   31 |     const samples = [];
   32 |     for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
   33 |       await page.waitForTimeout(500);
   34 |       samples.push(
   35 |         await page.evaluate(() => ({
   36 |           diagnostics: window.__POCKET__.diagnostics,
   37 |           children: window.__POCKET__.scene.children,
   38 |           heap: performance.memory?.usedJSHeapSize ?? null,
   39 |         })),
   40 |       );
   41 |     }
   42 |     await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
   43 |     await page
   44 |       .getByRole("button", { name: "Back to all games", exact: true })
   45 |       .click();
   46 |     const cleanup = await page.evaluate(() => window.__POCKET__.scene);
   47 |     if (cleanup.inputListeners !== 0)
   48 |       throw new Error(`${name}: leaked host input`);
   49 |     results.push({ name, samples, cleanup });
   50 |   }
   51 |   if (errors.length) throw new Error(errors.join("\n"));
   52 |   const report = {
   53 |     environment:
   54 |       "Headless desktop Chrome, 412×915 touch viewport, DPR 1, development build. Short diagnostic samples, not Android hardware or long-session certification.",
   55 |     measuredAt: new Date().toISOString(),
   56 |     results,
   57 |   };
   58 |   await writeFile(
   59 |     "docs/expansion-performance.json",
   60 |     JSON.stringify(report, null, 2) + "\n",
   61 |   );
   62 |   console.log(
   63 |     JSON.stringify(
   64 |       results.map(({ name, samples, cleanup }) => ({
   65 |         name,
   66 |         fps: samples.map((s) => Math.round(s.diagnostics.fps)),
   67 |         finalFrameMs: samples.at(-1).diagnostics.frameMs,
   68 |         children: samples.map((s) => s.children),
   69 |         inputListenersAfterExit: cleanup.inputListeners,
   70 |       })),
   71 |       null,
   72 |       2,
   73 |     ),
   74 |   );
   75 | } finally {
   76 |   await browser.close();
   77 | }

## scripts/offline-plugin.ts
SHA-256: c012a84e50db4ab8475780e3a58eae2b1c929a3f50c1165a0fd3cedd16378492
~~~text
    1 | import type { Plugin } from "vite";
    2 | import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
    3 | /** Cache only the shell on install. Game chunks are cached on demand or by an explicit download. */
    4 | export function offlinePlugin(): Plugin {
    5 |   return {
    6 |     name: "pocket-offline",
    7 |     apply: "build",
    8 |     generateBundle(_options, bundle) {
    9 |       const files = [
   10 |           "./",
   11 |           "./index.html",
   12 |           "./icon.svg",
   13 |           ...Object.keys(bundle).map((f) => "./" + f),
   14 |         ],
   15 |         initial = new Set<string>(["./", "./index.html", "./icon.svg"]);
   16 |       const visit = (name: string) => {
   17 |         if (initial.has("./" + name)) return;
   18 |         initial.add("./" + name);
   19 |         const chunk = bundle[name];
   20 |         if (chunk?.type === "chunk") {
   21 |           chunk.imports.forEach(visit);
   22 |           const css=(chunk as typeof chunk & {viteMetadata?:{importedCss:Set<string>}}).viteMetadata?.importedCss;
   23 |           css?.forEach(file=>initial.add("./"+file));
   24 |         }
   25 |       };
   26 |       for (const item of Object.values(bundle)) {
   27 |         if (item.type === "chunk" && item.isEntry) visit(item.fileName);
   28 |         if (/\/(nunito-sans|fredoka)-.*\.woff2$/.test(item.fileName))
   29 |           initial.add("./" + item.fileName);
   30 |       }
   31 |       const version = createHash("sha256")
   32 |         .update(JSON.stringify(Object.keys(bundle)))
   33 |         .digest("hex")
   34 |         .slice(0, 12);
   35 |       this.emitFile({
   36 |         type: "asset",
   37 |         fileName: "sw.js",
   38 |         source: `
   39 | const CACHE='pocket-rivals-${version}';
   40 | const FILES=${JSON.stringify([...new Set(files)])};
   41 | const SHELL=${JSON.stringify([...initial])};
   42 | const ALLOWED=new Set(FILES.map(f=>new URL(f,self.location.href).href));
   43 | self.addEventListener('install',event=>event.waitUntil(caches.open(CACHE).then(cache=>cache.addAll(SHELL)).then(()=>self.skipWaiting())));
   44 | self.addEventListener('activate',event=>event.waitUntil(caches.keys().then(keys=>Promise.all(keys.filter(key=>key.startsWith('pocket-rivals-')&&key!==CACHE).map(key=>caches.delete(key)))).then(()=>self.clients.claim())));
   45 | self.addEventListener('message',event=>{if(event.data?.type!=='CACHE_ALL')return;event.waitUntil(caches.open(CACHE).then(cache=>cache.addAll(FILES)).then(()=>event.ports[0]?.postMessage({ok:true}),()=>event.ports[0]?.postMessage({ok:false})));});
   46 | self.addEventListener('fetch',event=>{if(event.request.method!=='GET'||new URL(event.request.url).origin!==self.location.origin)return;event.respondWith((async()=>{const cache=await caches.open(CACHE),hit=await cache.match(event.request,{ignoreVary:true});if(hit)return hit;const response=await fetch(event.request);if(response.ok&&ALLOWED.has(event.request.url))await cache.put(event.request,response.clone());return response;})());});
   47 | `,
   48 |       });
   49 |     },
   50 |   };
   51 | }
~~~

## scripts/verify-math-bank.py
SHA-256: 334510d339caa81375634c8199be2af84737c86634a3d8e6443ab183740ec6c2
~~~text
    1 | """Generate 100 compact questions and independently evaluate each stated operation with SymPy.
    2 | Run in a development venv containing SymPy. No Python runtime ships with the game.
    3 | """
    4 | from pathlib import Path
    5 | import json, hashlib
    6 | import sympy as s
    7 | x=s.symbols('x',real=True); n=s.symbols('n',integer=True,positive=True)
    8 | rows=[]; evidence=[]
    9 | def add(family,k,topic,question,expected,computed,explanation,seconds=12,difficulty='medium',options=None):
   10 |     expected=s.sympify(expected); computed=s.simplify(computed)
   11 |     assert s.simplify(expected-computed)==0,(family,k,expected,computed)
   12 |     opts=options or [expected,expected+1,expected-1]
   13 |     opts=[s.sympify(v) for v in opts]
   14 |     assert all(s.simplify(opts[i]-opts[j])!=0 for i in range(3) for j in range(i))
   15 |     correct=len(rows)%3;opts[0],opts[correct]=opts[correct],opts[0]
   16 |     uid=f'{family}-{k}'
   17 |     rows.append(dict(id=uid,topic=topic,difficulty=difficulty,questionLatex=question,optionsLatex=[s.latex(v) for v in opts],correctIndex=correct,explanationLatex=explanation,estimatedSeconds=seconds))
   18 |     evidence.append(dict(id=uid,computed=str(computed),expected=str(expected),distinctOptions=True,verified=True))
   19 | for k in range(2,6):
   20 |     add('log-chain',k,'Derivatives',rf'\left.\frac{{d}}{{dx}}\ln(1+{k}x)\right|_{{x=0}}',k,s.diff(s.log(1+k*x),x).subs(x,0),rf'\frac{{{k}}}{{1+{k}x}}\bigg|_{{0}}={k}')
   21 |     add('power-at-one',k,'Derivatives',rf'\left.\frac{{d}}{{dx}}x^{{{k}}}\right|_{{x=1}}',k,s.diff(x**k,x).subs(x,1),rf'{k}x^{{{k-1}}}\big|_1={k}',8,'easy')
   22 |     add('exp-curvature',k,'Derivatives',rf'\left.\frac{{d^2}}{{dx^2}}e^{{{k}x}}\right|_{{x=0}}',k*k,s.diff(s.exp(k*x),x,2).subs(x,0),rf'{k}^2e^{{{k}x}}\big|_0={k*k}')
   23 |     add('sine-chain',k,'Derivatives',rf'\left.\frac{{d}}{{dx}}\sin({k}x)\right|_{{x=0}}',k,s.diff(s.sin(k*x),x).subs(x,0),rf'{k}\cos(0)={k}',8,'easy')
   24 |     add('product-log',k,'Derivatives',rf'\left.\frac{{d}}{{dx}}(x^{{{k}}}\ln x)\right|_{{x=1}}',1,s.diff(x**k*s.log(x),x).subs(x,1),r'\ln1=0,\quad x^{k-1}|_1=1',16)
   25 |     add('cosine-limit',k,'Limits',rf'\lim_{{x\to0}}\frac{{1-\cos({k}x)}}{{x^2}}',s.Rational(k*k,2),s.limit((1-s.cos(k*x))/x**2,x,0),rf'1-\cos({k}x)\sim\frac{{{k*k}x^2}}{{2}}',20,'hard')
   26 |     add('exp-sine-limit',k,'Limits',rf'\lim_{{x\to0}}\frac{{e^{{{k}x}}-1}}{{\sin x}}',k,s.limit((s.exp(k*x)-1)/s.sin(x),x,0),rf'e^{{{k}x}}-1\sim{k}x,\quad\sin x\sim x',15)
   27 |     add('root-limit',k,'Limits',rf'\lim_{{x\to0}}\frac{{\sqrt{{1+{k}x}}-1}}{{x}}',s.Rational(k,2),s.limit((s.sqrt(1+k*x)-1)/x,x,0),rf'\frac{{{k}}}{{\sqrt{{1+{k}x}}+1}}\to\frac{{{k}}}{{2}}',16)
   28 |     add('exponential-limit',k,'Limits',rf'\lim_{{x\to0}}(1+{k}x)^{{1/x}}',s.exp(k),s.exp(s.limit(s.log(1+k*x)/x,x,0)),rf'\ln L=\lim_{{x\to0}}\frac{{\ln(1+{k}x)}}{{x}}={k}',20,'hard',options=[s.exp(k),s.exp(k-1),s.exp(k+1)])
   29 |     add('odd-integral',k,'Integrals',rf'\int_{{-{k}}}^{{{k}}}\frac{{x^3}}{{1+x^2}}\,dx',0,s.integrate(x**3/(1+x*x),(x,-k,k)),r'\text{Odd function on a symmetric interval: }0',10,'easy')
   30 |     add('sine-square',k,'Integrals',rf'\int_0^\pi\sin^2({k}x)\,dx',s.pi/2,s.integrate(s.sin(k*x)**2,(x,0,s.pi)),r'\sin^2 u=\frac{1-\cos2u}{2}',18,options=[s.pi/2,s.pi,2*s.pi])
   31 |     add('power-integral',k,'Integrals',rf'\int_0^1{k}x^{{{k-1}}}\,dx',1,s.integrate(k*x**(k-1),(x,0,1)),rf'[x^{{{k}}}]_0^1=1',8,'easy')
   32 |     add('exp-integral',k,'Integrals',rf'\int_0^{{\ln {k}}}e^x\,dx',k-1,s.integrate(s.exp(x),(x,0,s.log(k))),rf'e^{{\ln {k}}}-e^0={k}-1',12)
   33 |     # These algebra questions specify real domains and have domain-independent answers.
   34 |     add('reciprocal-square',k,'Algebra',rf'\begin{{gathered}}x\in\mathbb R\setminus\{{0\}},\ x+\frac1x={k}\\x^2+\frac1{{x^2}}=?\end{{gathered}}',k*k-2,s.simplify(s.solve(x*x-k*x+1,x)[0]**2+1/s.solve(x*x-k*x+1,x)[0]**2),rf'(x+1/x)^2-2={k*k-2}',18)
   35 |     roots=s.solve(x*x-k*x+1,x)
   36 |     add('vieta-square',k,'Algebra',rf'\begin{{gathered}}\alpha,\beta:\ x^2-{k}x+1=0\\\alpha^2+\beta^2=?\end{{gathered}}',k*k-2,sum(r*r*m for r,m in s.roots(x*x-k*x+1).items()),rf'(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta={k}^2-2',18)
   37 |     add('geometric-series',k,'Algebra',rf'\sum_{{n=1}}^\infty\left(\frac1{{{k}}}\right)^n',s.Rational(1,k-1),s.summation(s.Rational(1,k)**n,(n,1,s.oo)),rf'\frac{{1/{k}}}{{1-1/{k}}}=\frac1{{{k-1}}}',15)
   38 |     add('log-power',k,'Algebra',rf'\log_{{{k}}}\left({k}^{{{k+1}}}\right)',k+1,s.log(k**(k+1))/s.log(k),rf'\log_a(a^m)=m={k+1}',8,'easy')
   39 |     mat=s.Matrix([[k,1],[k+1,1]])
   40 |     add('det-difference',k,'Matrices',rf'\det\begin{{pmatrix}}{k}&1\\{k+1}&1\end{{pmatrix}}',-1,mat.det(),rf'{k}-({k+1})=-1',10,'easy')
   41 |     add('det-scalar',k,'Matrices',rf'\begin{{gathered}}A\in\mathbb R^{{2\times2}},\ \det A={k}\\\det(2A)=?\end{{gathered}}',4*k,(2*s.Matrix([[k,0],[0,1]])).det(),rf'\det(2A)=2^2\det A={4*k}',20,'hard')
   42 |     add('det-triangle',k,'Matrices',rf'\det\begin{{pmatrix}}{k}&2\\0&{k+1}\end{{pmatrix}}',k*(k+1),s.Matrix([[k,2],[0,k+1]]).det(),rf'{k}\cdot{k+1}-0={k*(k+1)}',10,'easy')
   43 |     add('i-cycle',k,'Complex numbers',rf'i^2=-1.\quad i^{{{4*k+2}}}=?',-1,s.I**(4*k+2),r'i^{4m+2}=i^2=-1',10,'easy')
   44 |     add('modulus-square',k,'Complex numbers',rf'i^2=-1.\quad|{k}+{k}i|^2=?',2*k*k,s.Abs(k+k*s.I)**2,rf'{k}^2+{k}^2={2*k*k}',12)
   45 |     j=k-1
   46 |     add('complex-real',k,'Complex numbers',rf'i^2=-1.\quad\operatorname{{Re}}(1+i)^{{{2*j}}}=?',s.re((2*s.I)**j),s.re(s.expand((1+s.I)**(2*j))),rf'(1+i)^2=2i,\quad\operatorname{{Re}}(2i)^{{{j}}}={s.latex(s.re((2*s.I)**j))}',22,'hard')
   47 |     add('coin-one-head',k,'Probability',rf'\begin{{gathered}}\text{{{k} fair independent coin flips}}\\P(\text{{exactly 1 head}})=?\end{{gathered}}',s.Rational(k,2**k),s.binomial(k,1)*s.Rational(1,2)**k,rf'\binom{{{k}}}1/2^{{{k}}}={s.latex(s.Rational(k,2**k))}',15,options=[s.Rational(k,2**k),s.Rational(k+1,2**k),s.Rational(k-1,2**k)])
   48 |     q=k+2
   49 |     add('choose-pair',k,'Probability',rf'\binom{{{q}}}2',q*(q-1)//2,s.binomial(q,2),rf'\frac{{{q}\cdot{q-1}}}2={q*(q-1)//2}',10,'easy')
   50 | assert len(rows)==100 and len({r['id'] for r in rows})==100 and len({r['questionLatex'] for r in rows})==100
   51 | root=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
   52 | out=root/'src/games/math-quiz/questions/university.json'
   53 | out.write_text(json.dumps(rows,indent=2)+'\n')
   54 | report=dict(count=len(rows),engine='SymPy '+s.__version__,method='Symbolic derivatives, limits, integrals, matrix determinants, exact identities and combinatorial formulas; all distractors checked pairwise.',independentHumanReview=False,mentalTime='Editorial estimates; not measured with students.',sha256=hashlib.sha256(out.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),results=evidence)
   55 | (root/'docs/math-validation.json').write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2)+'\n')
   56 | print('Verified 100 answer keys, 300 pairwise option distinctions, and 100 unique IDs/statements.')

## src/arcade/snake/AGENTS.md
SHA-256: 81ebad13cf94933381ac74acf1fdd05d5c3191e3e163332faaa7cc19fa94913e
~~~text
    1 | # Solo arcade module
    2 | 
    3 | SnakeRules.ts owns the grid, fixed movement interval, two-direction input queue, safe tail movement and food spawning. SnakeGame.ts only renders/interpolates and maps pad/swipe/keyboard input. Keep movement deterministic under different render rates. Pause clears queued directions. Report finishArcade; never duel points.
    4 | 
    5 | Use only this module and shared contracts/helpers. Phaser owns the render loop; use fixed stepping and host-cleaned inputs. Relevant checks: tests/unit/phase3.test.ts and tests/browser/phase3.spec.ts. Arcade metadata must exclude tournaments.
~~~

SHA-256: d88893c93f7de8e068e852c214aec6fe08fa11e4c84b75938a9e578a5d5bdba6

    1 | import type Phaser from "phaser";
    2 | import type { GameContext, MiniGame } from "../../shared/contracts/GameModule";
    3 | import { theme } from "../../core/ThemeManager";
    4 | import { rounded, circle, label } from "../../shared/components/drawing";
    5 | import { SnakeWorld, type Direction } from "./SnakeRules";
    6 | export class SnakeGame implements MiniGame {
    7 |   private ctx!: GameContext;
    8 |   private world = new SnakeWorld();
    9 |   private g!: Phaser.GameObjects.Graphics;
   10 |   private labels: Phaser.GameObjects.Text[] = [];
   11 |   private keys = new Set<string>();
   12 |   private pressed = new Set<string>();
   13 |   private paused = false;
   14 |   private reported = false;
   15 |   private age = 0;
   16 |   private start: { x: number; y: number } | null = null;
   17 |   initialize(ctx: GameContext) {
   18 |     this.ctx = ctx;
   19 |     this.g = ctx.scene.add.graphics();
   20 |     ctx.setHint("ARROWS OR WASD · SWIPE OR USE THE PAD");
   21 |     this.keys = ctx.input.keys([
   22 |       "ArrowUp",
   23 |       "ArrowDown",
   24 |       "ArrowLeft",
   25 |       "ArrowRight",
   26 |       "KeyW",
   27 |       "KeyA",
   28 |       "KeyS",
   29 |       "KeyD",
   30 |     ]);
   31 |     for (const [x, y, text] of [
   32 |       [210, 574, "↑"],
   33 |       [152, 620, "←"],
   34 |       [210, 620, "↓"],
   35 |       [268, 620, "→"],
   36 |     ] as const)
   37 |       this.labels.push(label(ctx.scene, x, y, text, 25));
   38 |     ctx.input.tap((x, y) => {
   39 |       if (this.paused) return;
   40 |       let dir: Direction | undefined;
   41 |       if (Math.abs(x - 210) < 24 && Math.abs(y - 574) < 23) dir = "up";
   42 |       else if (Math.abs(y - 620) < 24) {
   43 |         if (Math.abs(x - 152) < 24) dir = "left";
   44 |         if (Math.abs(x - 210) < 24) dir = "down";
   45 |         if (Math.abs(x - 268) < 24) dir = "right";
   46 |       }
   47 |       if (dir) this.world.steer(dir);
   48 |     });
   49 |     ctx.input.drag(
   50 |       (x, y) => {
   51 |         if (y < 130 || y > 550) return false;
   52 |         this.start = { x, y };
   53 |         return true;
   54 |       },
   55 |       () => {},
   56 |       (x, y) => {
   57 |         if (!this.start) return;
   58 |         const dx = x - this.start.x,
   59 |           dy = y - this.start.y;
   60 |         this.start = null;
   61 |         if (Math.hypot(dx, dy) > 15)
   62 |           this.world.steer(
   63 |             Math.abs(dx) > Math.abs(dy)
   64 |               ? dx > 0
   65 |                 ? "right"
   66 |                 : "left"
   67 |               : dy > 0
   68 |                 ? "down"
   69 |                 : "up",
   70 |           );
   71 |       },
   72 |       () => {
   73 |         this.start = null;
   74 |       },
   75 |     );
   76 |   }
   77 |   update(dt: number) {
   78 |     if (this.paused) return;
   79 |     this.age += dt;
   80 |     const map: Record<string, Direction> = {
   81 |       ArrowUp: "up",
   82 |       KeyW: "up",
   83 |       ArrowDown: "down",
   84 |       KeyS: "down",
   85 |       ArrowLeft: "left",
   86 |       KeyA: "left",
   87 |       ArrowRight: "right",
   88 |       KeyD: "right",
   89 |     };
   90 |     for (const key of this.keys)
   91 |       if (!this.pressed.has(key)) this.world.steer(map[key]);
   92 |     this.pressed = new Set(this.keys);
   93 |     const before = this.world.score;
   94 |     if (this.age > 0.6) this.world.update(dt);
   95 |     if (this.world.score > before) this.ctx.audio.play("goal");
   96 |     const w = this.world,
   97 |       g = this.g;
   98 |     g.clear();
   99 |     rounded(g, 24, 112, 372, 538, 20, theme.green, 4);
  100 |     rounded(g, 38, 138, 344, 404, 8, 0xdde9c4, 3);
  101 |     g.fillStyle(theme.ink, 0.08);
  102 |     for (let y = 0; y < 20; y++)
  103 |       for (let x = 0; x < 17; x++) g.fillCircle(50 + x * 20, 150 + y * 20, 1);
  104 |     const t = Math.min(1, w.accumulator / w.interval);
  105 |     for (let i = w.body.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
  106 |       const c = w.body[i],
  107 |         old = w.previous[i] ?? c,
  108 |         x = 50 + (old.x + (c.x - old.x) * t) * 20,
  109 |         y = 150 + (old.y + (c.y - old.y) * t) * 20;
  110 |       rounded(g, x - 9, y - 9, 18, 18, 5, i ? theme.blue : theme.orange, 2);
  111 |       if (i === 0) {
  112 |         const vertical = w.direction === "up" || w.direction === "down";
  113 |         for (const side of [-1, 1])
  114 |           g.fillStyle(theme.ink).fillCircle(
  115 |             x + (vertical ? side * 4 : w.direction === "right" ? 4 : -4),
  116 |             y + (vertical ? (w.direction === "down" ? 4 : -4) : side * 4),
  117 |             2,
  118 |           );
  119 |       }
  120 |     }
  121 |     if (w.food) {
  122 |       circle(g, 50 + w.food.x * 20, 150 + w.food.y * 20, 6, theme.orange, 2);
  123 |       g.lineStyle(2, theme.ink).lineBetween(
  124 |         51 + w.food.x * 20,
  125 |         143 + w.food.y * 20,
  126 |         54 + w.food.x * 20,
  127 |         140 + w.food.y * 20,
  128 |       );
  129 |     }
  130 |     for (const [x, y] of [
  131 |       [210, 574],
  132 |       [152, 620],
  133 |       [210, 620],
  134 |       [268, 620],
  135 |     ])
  136 |       rounded(g, x - 24, y - 22, 48, 44, 12, theme.white, 2);
  137 |     this.ctx.setArcadeHUD(
  138 |       w.score,
  139 |       `LEVEL ${1 + Math.floor(w.score / 50)} · ${w.body.length} LITTLE SQUARES`,
  140 |     );
  141 |     if (w.dead && !this.reported) {
  142 |       this.reported = true;
  143 |       this.ctx.audio.play("draw");
  144 |       this.ctx.finishArcade(
  145 |         w.score,
  146 |         w.won ? "You filled the whole garden." : "A little longer next time.",
  147 |       );
  148 |     }
  149 |   }
  150 |   pause() {
  151 |     this.paused = true;
  152 |     this.world.clearInput();
  153 |     this.pressed.clear();
  154 |     this.start = null;
  155 |   }
  156 |   resume() {
  157 |     this.paused = false;
  158 |     this.age = 0;
  159 |   }
  160 |   dispose() {
  161 |     this.g.destroy();
  162 |     this.labels.forEach((l) => l.destroy());
  163 |   }
  164 |   snapshot() {
  165 |     return {
  166 |       body: this.world.body.map((c) => ({ ...c })),
  167 |       food: this.world.food,
  168 |       score: this.world.score,
  169 |       dead: this.world.dead,
  170 |       direction: this.world.direction,
  171 |     };
  172 |   }
  173 | }

## src/arcade/snake/SnakeRules.ts
SHA-256: e3d0866960c15e4778388c41787bf2bb0332ff75197a2566df9832bf75edea16
~~~text
    1 | export type Direction = "up" | "right" | "down" | "left";
    2 | export interface Cell {
    3 |   x: number;
    4 |   y: number;
    5 | }
    6 | const vectors: Record<Direction, Cell> = {
    7 |   up: { x: 0, y: -1 },
    8 |   right: { x: 1, y: 0 },
    9 |   down: { x: 0, y: 1 },
   10 |   left: { x: -1, y: 0 },
   11 | };
   12 | export class SnakeWorld {
   13 |   readonly width = 17;
   14 |   readonly height = 20;
   15 |   body: Cell[] = [
   16 |     { x: 8, y: 11 },
   17 |     { x: 7, y: 11 },
   18 |     { x: 6, y: 11 },
   19 |   ];
   20 |   previous: Cell[] = this.body.map((c) => ({ ...c }));
   21 |   direction: Direction = "right";
   22 |   food: Cell | null = null;
   23 |   score = 0;
   24 |   dead = false;
   25 |   won = false;
   26 |   private queue: Direction[] = [];
   27 |   accumulator = 0;
   28 |   constructor(private random = Math.random) {
   29 |     this.spawnFood();
   30 |   }
   31 |   get interval() {
   32 |     return Math.max(0.065, 0.18 - this.score * 0.0015);
   33 |   }
   34 |   steer(dir: Direction) {
   35 |     const last = this.queue.at(-1) ?? this.direction,
   36 |       a = vectors[last],
   37 |       b = vectors[dir];
   38 |     if (
   39 |       this.queue.length >= 2 ||
   40 |       last === dir ||
   41 |       (a.x + b.x === 0 && a.y + b.y === 0)
   42 |     )
   43 |       return false;
   44 |     this.queue.push(dir);
   45 |     return true;
   46 |   }
   47 |   clearInput() {
   48 |     this.queue = [];
   49 |   }
   50 |   update(dt: number) {
   51 |     if (this.dead) return;
   52 |     this.accumulator += Math.max(0, Math.min(dt, 0.5));
   53 |     while (this.accumulator >= this.interval && !this.dead) {
   54 |       this.accumulator -= this.interval;
   55 |       this.tick();
   56 |     }
   57 |   }
   58 |   tick() {
   59 |     if (this.dead) return;
   60 |     this.direction = this.queue.shift() ?? this.direction;
   61 |     const d = vectors[this.direction],
   62 |       head = { x: this.body[0].x + d.x, y: this.body[0].y + d.y },
   63 |       eating = head.x === this.food?.x && head.y === this.food?.y,
   64 |       solid = eating ? this.body : this.body.slice(0, -1);
   65 |     if (
   66 |       head.x < 0 ||
   67 |       head.x >= this.width ||
   68 |       head.y < 0 ||
   69 |       head.y >= this.height ||
   70 |       solid.some((c) => c.x === head.x && c.y === head.y)
   71 |     ) {
   72 |       this.dead = true;
   73 |       return;
   74 |     }
   75 |     this.previous = this.body.map((c) => ({ ...c }));
   76 |     this.body.unshift(head);
   77 |     if (eating) {
   78 |       this.score += 10;
   79 |       this.spawnFood();
   80 |     } else this.body.pop();
   81 |   }
   82 |   spawnFood() {
   83 |     const free: Cell[] = [];
   84 |     for (let y = 0; y < this.height; y++)
   85 |       for (let x = 0; x < this.width; x++)
   86 |         if (!this.body.some((c) => c.x === x && c.y === y)) free.push({ x, y });
   87 |     if (!free.length) {
   88 |       this.food = null;
   89 |       this.dead = this.won = true;
   90 |       return;
   91 |     }
   92 |     this.food =
   93 |       free[Math.min(free.length - 1, Math.floor(this.random() * free.length))];
   94 |   }
   95 | }
~~~

## src/arcade/space-shooter/AGENTS.md
SHA-256: a4e14d062140921256f683a06653f8d4e0450a4729a2b2d3f044a8956caffd40
~~~text
    1 | # Solo arcade module
    2 | 
    3 | ShooterWorld.ts owns fixed-step combat, swept segment collisions, damage immunity and bounded pools (80 projectiles, 8 pickups, 24 effects). Waves.ts defines formations, enemy types and difficulty progression. Powerups.ts owns gear metadata and rare-life eligibility. ShooterArt.ts draws original vectors; SpaceShooterGame.ts binds host inputs, HUD, audio and cleanup. Report finishArcade; never duel points.
    4 | 
    5 | Gold supply ships drop actual falling capsules; ordinary kills periodically add loot. Catching capsules upgrades cannons or grants timed lasers, rapid fire, wingmates and shields. Extra lives are milestone-only with a cooldown/cap; never add them to ordinary random loot. Preserve player/enemy projectile reservations and per-projectile piercing hit history. Use seeded random injection for tests. No additional render loops or timers.
    6 | 
    7 | Use only this module and shared contracts/helpers. Phaser owns the render loop; use fixed stepping and host-cleaned inputs. Relevant checks: tests/unit/star-patrol.test.ts, tests/unit/phase3.test.ts, tests/browser/star-patrol.spec.ts and tests/browser/phase3.spec.ts. Arcade metadata must exclude tournaments. See docs/STAR_PATROL.md for tuning and verification.
~~~

    1 | export type PowerupKind =
    2 |   "spread" | "rapid" | "laser" | "drone" | "shield" | "life";
    3 | export const POWERUPS: Record<
    4 |   PowerupKind,
    5 |   { name: string; color: number; duration: number }
    6 | > = {
    7 |   spread: { name: "CANNON UPGRADE", color: 0xf5ad69, duration: 0 },
    8 |   rapid: { name: "RAPID FIRE", color: 0xf2ce72, duration: 14 },
    9 |   laser: { name: "PIERCING LASER", color: 0x76c8db, duration: 16 },
   10 |   drone: { name: "WINGMATES", color: 0xb2a0d1, duration: 18 },
   11 |   shield: { name: "SHIELD READY", color: 0x81bdc1, duration: 0 },
   12 |   life: { name: "+1 LIFE", color: 0xe4a9b4, duration: 0 },
   13 | };
   14 | export interface Pickup {
   15 |   id: number;
   16 |   x: number;
   17 |   y: number;
   18 |   kind: PowerupKind;
   19 |   active: boolean;
   20 |   age: number;
   21 | }
   22 | export function waveReward(wave: number): PowerupKind {
   23 |   return (["spread", "rapid", "drone", "laser", "shield"] as const)[
   24 |     (wave - 1) % 5
   25 |   ];
   26 | }
   27 | /** Extra lives are exclusive to six-level milestones, never ordinary random loot. */
   28 | export function canDropLife(
   29 |   wave: number,
   30 |   elapsed: number,
   31 |   lastDrop: number,
   32 |   lives: number,
   33 | ) {
   34 |   return wave % 6 === 0 && elapsed - lastDrop >= 90 && lives < 4;
   35 | }
